description:
**Surfaced 2026-05-17 by PLINY at Arc 35 close + user-tier POLYBIUS QA pass.**

Two small follow-ups from Arc 35 (stoa--kjo) shipping. Neither affects shipped substrate canon — both are housekeeping on artifacts that surround the canon. Bundled because both surfaced from the same arc-35 retro and both are P4 hygiene (PLINY tagged "P5" in verdict text — bw scale tops at P4, treat as floor).

## Item 1 — Future-arc directive cleanup: broken `substrate/CLAUDE.md` path-citation

**Empirical anchor:** ARGUS F1 against `agents/design/stoa--kjo/design.md` rev1 — surfaced that `substrate/arcs/arc-35-build-directive.md` lines 118 + 183 + the polybius-activation paste line 36 cite `substrate/CLAUDE.md` as the project-tier rule file. That path does not exist: the project-tier CLAUDE.md is at `/CLAUDE.md` (repo root); no `substrate/CLAUDE.md` exists. DAEDALUS rev2 corrected the error in every SHIPPED wording (the §28.4 body in operating-disciplines.md cites "project-tier `CLAUDE.md` (at the project repo root)" — verified live 2026-05-17). Substrate canon does NOT propagate the error.

The error survives in the on-disk arc-35 dispatch artifacts (`substrate/arcs/arc-35-build-directive.md` + `HUMAN_paste-polybius-arc-35-instruction.md` — already moved to `substrate/arcs/arc-35/pastes/` per §5.11; verify post-archival) AND likely in some prior arc directives that copy-pasted the same field-name pattern. Spot-check on dispatch:

- `substrate/arcs/arc-35-build-directive.md` lines 118 + 183 (confirmed)
- Other arc directives — sweep with `grep -rn "substrate/CLAUDE.md" substrate/arcs/`

**Fix shape:** sweep + correct each occurrence to either `/CLAUDE.md` (repo root) or `CLAUDE.md (at the project repo root)`. No substrate canon change needed (the canon already has the corrected wording). Direct-to-main user-tier housekeeping commit per `MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` §18.1 if scope stays small (sweep + edit + commit + push); larger sweep may warrant a small arc if it surfaces wider documentation drift.

**Why low priority:** historical dispatch artifacts are reference material, not load-bearing for any future read path. Substrate canon (the file future agents actually consume) is correct. The cleanup prevents the same broken path being copy-pasted into future arc directives — a soft prevention, not a hard fix.

## Item 2 — Arc 35 design-probe refinement (`agents/design/stoa--kjo/design.md`)

**Empirical anchor:** VERA verdict on Arc 35 build flagged two probe-formulation methodology concerns:
- §4.6 squash-merge probe command includes a `main` revspec that's not strictly needed for the trailer-preservation property check — drop it for cleaner future-probe-reuse.
- §4.4 expectation phrasing uses "distinct grep-line-count" which can over-count when a single canonical citation appears on multiple lines within the same paragraph; should be "distinct-cite-count" (unique citation strings) for the property the probe actually tests.

**Fix shape:** edit-only revision to `agents/design/stoa--kjo/design.md` §4.4 + §4.6. Design doc is post-build reference (VERA already ran the probes; shipping is complete), so this is documentation hygiene that improves probe-reuse for future arcs that pattern-match Arc 35's verification approach. Direct-to-main per §18.1.

**Why low priority:** the probes WORKED (VERA exercised them; ZENO ran 7/7 mechanical checks; Arc 35 shipped clean). The methodology concerns are about future probe-reuse, not about Arc 35 correctness.

## Sequencing

Two small edits. Could do both in a single direct-to-main housekeeping commit (a single sweep across arc-35-build-directive.md + design.md + any prior-arc occurrences found by Item 1's grep sweep). Or could defer to a small canonification batch later if more substrate-doc hygiene items accrue.
